description: Results of five synthetic canary scenarios validating provider-fallback circuit-breaker behaviour.

canaries.name: Provider-wide daily quota exhaustion
canaries.scenario: Inject HTTP 429 with error_code=free-models-per-day remaining=0 from primary provider for all models.
canaries.expected: Provider circuit opens immediately; zero same-provider retries; task routed to next eligible provider.
canaries.notes: Replicates MSG231 incident. Zero same-provider retries confirmed.

canaries.name: Model-only quota failure preserves provider eligibility
canaries.scenario: Inject HTTP 429 scoped to one model; all other models on provider remain healthy.
canaries.expected: Model circuit opens; provider circuit remains closed; another model on same provider selected.

canaries.name: Oversized context routes to larger-context model
canaries.scenario: Submit task with 80,000 tokens to model with 32,000-token context window.
canaries.expected: CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE classified; context compaction attempted; if insufficient, route to model with sufficient context window.

canaries.name: No eligible route emits BLOCKED receipt
canaries.scenario: All configured providers and models suppressed simultaneously.
canaries.expected: BLOCKED receipt emitted; mission queue position preserved; no task dropped.

canaries.name: Transient rate limit bounded retry then failover
canaries.scenario: Inject HTTP 429 with Retry-After on primary provider; three retries exhaust budget; route to secondary provider.
canaries.expected: Maximum 3 jittered retries on same provider; then failover to next eligible provider.
